attributes.residual: STRUCTURAL, single named mechanism: MWCC lowers `if (cond) return <value>;` at these two sites as a two-instruction `beq <fallthrough>; b <epilogue>` pair instead of the target's single `bne <epilogue>`, costing one net instruction (T149/O150). The third early-out in the same function, `if (!ret) return ret;` at the bottom of the for(;;), FUSES correctly in both builds -- and the reason is visible in the aligned view: there the return is the FALLTHROUGH path and the conditional branch is the loop backedge, so no forward branch to the epilogue is needed at all. That polarity asymmetry inside one function is the useful observation: the unfused pair appears only where the early-out requires a FORWARD transfer to the epilogue. Verified our `b` lands directly on the epilogue (fnasm --ours: 0x23c = `lwz r0,148(r1)`), so there is no shared exit stub to eliminate. Third cluster still open: target keeps an extra `addi` at T[90]@0x168. UNPARK CONDITION: a spelling that makes MWCC emit a direct conditional branch to the epilogue for a value-returning forward early-out; both recorded guard-shape spellings are byte-identical no-ops, so the next attempt must change the CFG, not the guard text.
